ModMetadata.Name: Server Integrity
ModMetadata.Author: Piyper
ModMetadata.Description:
[h1]Server Integrity[/h1]
[img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/piyper/stationeers-server-integrity/main/About/WorkshopImages/01-integrity-scanner-overview.png[/img] [img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/piyper/stationeers-server-integrity/main/About/WorkshopImages/02-integrity-scanner-connected.png[/img] [img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/piyper/stationeers-server-integrity/main/About/WorkshopImages/03-integrity-gun-popup.png[/img]
[b]BETA RELEASE:[/b] I have tried to consider every test case and fix every bug I could find, but there is no guarantee that this release is perfect. Please report bugs as you find them, and I will do my best to fix them.
[b]Artwork note:[/b] I am not a graphic artist—and I am actually quite bad at it—so I cloned existing Stationeers objects to create the new items. If you would like to help create original artwork, please let me know.
Server Integrity gives multiplayer communities practical tools to protect player builds from unauthorized damage, deconstruction, ownership changes, and destructive console commands.
[h2]Integrity Gun[/h2]
[b]Multiplayer ownership rule:[/b] Unless you are a server administrator, the Integrity Gun changes only structures you own. Connected, matching, and blast-area modes skip structures owned by other players.
[b]Ownership notice:[/b] Stationeers may occasionally record an object's ownership incorrectly. If the Integrity Gun does not recognize part of your build as yours, ask a server administrator to correct the structure's ownership.
Aim at a structure and hold the primary action until the progress bar completes. The gun changes protection according to its selected mode. Right-click cycles through the modes:
[list] [*][b]Toggle target[/b] — changes only the object being aimed at. [*][b]Toggle connected[/b] — changes the target and the construction connected to it. [*][b]Toggle matching[/b] — changes connected objects of the same type as the target. For example, targeting a window affects matching windows in that connected build without changing its frames. [*][b]Toggle blast areas[/b] — finds hazardous equipment associated with the connected build and changes the equipment and nearby structures together. This lets you restore normal explosion damage around furnaces or tanks, so you can preserve the real consequences of mistakes. [/list]
The action popup shows whether the current use will make the selected objects destructible or indestructible. Protected objects cannot be damaged or normally deconstructed. Changes persist when the world is saved and restarted.
On multiplayer servers, administrators may protect any structure. Other players may use the gun only on structures they own. Single-player users have unrestricted access.
[h2]Ownership Gun[/h2]
The Ownership Gun lets a server administrator assign a structure to a player. Label the gun with the intended online player's name and aim at the structure. Leaving the gun at its default name assigns ownership to the administrator using it.
Use the gun's selector to choose between changing only the target and changing its connected construction. The target popup reports the current owner by name when that owner can be identified. Ownership changes persist with the world save.
The Ownership Gun cannot be used by non-administrators on a multiplayer server. It is unrestricted in single-player.
[h2]Integrity Scanner SPU[/h2]
Insert the Integrity Scanner SPU into Sensor Lenses and power them on to inspect nearby construction:
[list] [*][b]Red[/b] — protected from damage and deconstruction. [*][b]Green[/b] — normal damage and deconstruction are enabled. [/list]
This provides a quick visual check of a protected build and makes gaps in its protection easier to find.
[h2]Additional server protection[/h2]
The mod prevents non-administrators from using mutating thing console commands such as spawning and deleting objects. This closes an easy route around normal building and ownership rules while leaving non-mutating commands available.
Server Integrity is intended to deter common griefing on community servers. It does not replace access control: hazardous machinery, printers, consoles, and security equipment should still be kept behind secured doors where appropriate.
[h2]Manufacturing and installation[/h2]
The Integrity Gun, Ownership Gun, and Integrity Scanner SPU are available from the [b]Security Printer[/b]. Each recipe requires:
[list] [*]1 g gold [*]1 energy [*]10 seconds [/list]
The tools are also available through the creative spawn menu.
For multiplayer servers using Server Integrity, install the mod on the dedicated server and every connecting client. A client may leave the mod installed when joining servers that do not use it, but attempting to create one of the mod's items on such a server may produce an error.
ModMetadata.ChangeLog:
[h2]0.6.7[/h2] Completes the project rename to Server Integrity across the source folder, project, namespace, assembly, DLL, and log identity. The stable mod ID and item names are unchanged.
[h2]0.6.6[/h2] Toggle Blast Areas now discovers freestanding hazardous equipment within 6 metres of the selected connected construction before applying each hazard's 6-metre protection radius.
[h2]0.6.5[/h2] Toggle Blast Areas uses the connected construction to discover hazardous equipment, then toggles every structure within 6 metres of those hazards whether or not those nearby structures are connected.
[h2]0.6.4[/h2] Reduces the Toggle Blast Areas protection radius from 10 metres to 6 metres.
[h2]0.6.3[/h2] Avoids refreshing structure damage and rendering state during synchronization when the indestructible value has not changed.
[h2]0.6.2[/h2] Toggle Blast Areas now includes connected structures within 10 metres of each connected hazardous object instead of changing only the hazardous object itself.
[h2]0.6.1[/h2] Synchronizes the finalized Steam-ID owner after a newly placed structure is created so clients do not temporarily report owned objects as Unowned.
[h2]0.6.0[/h2] Replaces the Integrity Gun modes with Toggle Target, Toggle Connected, Toggle Matching, and Toggle Blast Areas. Connected and matching modes use the selected target as the declarative state; blast mode uses the first connected hazardous object. Matching continues to use the exact prefab hash.
[h2]0.5.4[/h2] Resolves saved Steam-ID ownership against loaded player bodies so the gun popup displays the owner's name correctly.
[h2]0.5.3[/h2] Stores Integrity Gun modes directly in the native saved mode field instead of the spray-gun animator, which always reset the value to zero.
[h2]0.5.2[/h2] Fixes mouse right-click mode cycling by updating during Stationeers' client-side secondary-use evaluation pass.
[h2]0.5.1[/h2] Moves Integrity Gun mode cycling to the actual active-tool toggle path used by right-click.
[h2]0.5.0[/h2] Adds four right-click Integrity Gun modes: protect connected, unprotect connected, hazard-aware protection with a 10 m exclusion around hazardous equipment, and matching-prefab protection within the connected construction.
[h2]0.4.22[/h2] Mutating thing-command denials no longer disclose administrator command or authentication details.
[h2]0.4.21[/h2] Fixed dedicated servers incorrectly treating all gun actions as single-player administrator actions.
[h2]0.4.20[/h2] Removes multiplayer host-status shortcuts from Ownership Gun authorization. Every multiplayer ownership change now requires a nonempty matching server auth secret; single-player remains unrestricted.
[h2]0.4.19[/h2] Restores Stationeers' delayed-action completion guard inside the Harmony prefix so gun mutations and RPCs occur only after the progress bar reaches completion.
[h2]0.4.18[/h2] Network clients now always submit gun actions to the authoritative server instead of incorrectly taking the local single-player action path.
[h2]0.4.17[/h2] Uses the actual network role instead of the unreliable batch-mode flag when distinguishing a local host from a dedicated-server client for administrator authorization.
[h2]0.4.16[/h2] Server Integrity is required when hosting a server and optional when loaded only as a client, allowing that client to join servers that do not run the mod.
[h2]0.4.15[/h2] Dedicated-server clients are no longer treated as administrators merely because the game marks them as host. Ownership Gun access now requires the matching server auth secret; single-player remains unrestricted.
[h2]0.4.14[/h2] Synchronizes restored ownership and indestructible state to each client after joining so gun popups and scanner lenses reflect the authoritative saved state.
[h2]0.4.13[/h2] Integrity and ownership changes now occur only after the tool's progress action completes, rather than immediately on the initial click.
[h3]Version 0.4.12[/h3] Removes Steam IDs from the ownership popup. Resolved owners display by name; unresolved owners display as Unknown owner.
[h3]Version 0.4.11[/h3] Blocks direct multiplayer-client use of the mutating thing spawn, spawnvel, and delete commands. Administrators retain access through the authenticated serverrun command; server console and single-player use remain unrestricted.
[h3]Version 0.4.10[/h3] Shows the selected target's current owner in the Integrity Gun and Ownership Gun action popup.
[h3]Version 0.4.9[/h3] Removes the inherited Spray Can slot from both custom gun prefabs and explicitly assigns all three Security Printer recipes to Tier One.
[h3]Version 0.4.8[/h3] Installs the authoritative Labeller rename-request guard after world loading so it cannot interfere with dedicated-server terrain startup.
[h3]Version 0.4.7[/h3] Renamed the mod to Server Integrity. Tool and item names are unchanged.
[h3]Version 0.4.6[/h3] Renamed the mod to Integrity. Tool and item names are unchanged.
[h3]Version 0.4.5[/h3] Indestructible objects can no longer be renamed with a Labeller or a forged rename request.
[h3]Version 0.4.4[/h3] An administrator using an Ownership Gun with its default label now assigns ownership to themselves.
[h3]Version 0.4.3[/h3] The Integrity Scanner SPU now uses the same Security Printer recipe as both custom guns.
[h3]Version 0.4.2[/h3] Both custom guns are now printed in the Security Printer from 1 g gold, using 1 energy over 10 seconds.
[h3]Version 0.4.1[/h3] The Integrity Gun and Ownership Gun no longer expose the inherited paint-can slot.
[h3]Version 0.4.0[/h3] Adds the Ownership Gun, server-authoritative ownership and integrity permissions, and a common placement fix that records Steam IDs instead of temporary brain reference IDs.
[h3]Version 0.3.1[/h3] Connected mode now bridges Stationeers' incomplete structural-neighbour graph using physical bounds contact, covering continuous frames, windows, faces, and attached construction pieces.
[h3]Version 0.3.0[/h3] Uses the Integrity Gun's On/Off selector as Target Only and Connected Construction modes. Connected mode follows structural neighbors and attached devices.
[h3]Version 0.2.1[/h3] Adds a 250 ms activation cooldown to prevent one click from toggling an object multiple times.
[h3]Version 0.2.0[/h3] Adds the Integrity Scanner SPU for Sensor Lenses.
[h3]Version 0.1.0[/h3] Initial release.
